Dead game, no updates in almost a year now, no dlc for longer than that, no info about this game from the devs for months only to post some stupid community post. should have been Sniper Elite 5 dlc....

Look, I normally really like the Sniper Elite franchise, ok? Like, I've spent literal days on individual maps trying to optimize my route, get achievements, find collectibles, and things like that in past SE games.

Sniper Elite Resistance is pretty bad.

It feels like an afterthought, as if the developers were like, "Hey, we have some European assets lying around, let's shove them onto some maps with half-assed buildings, missing polygons, and objects you should be able to move through or over but can't because reasons. Then we'll sprinkle a few bad guys here & there, create a new main character with annoying & repetitive lines, add a big bad with zero story (and a stupid death), invent another 'superweapon' threat with zero urgency (and a stupid name) and call it a day."

It's only worth buying if it's been *steeply* discounted, including the DLC, and even then only if you're really into the franchise.

Otherwise you're buying a game that is buggy as hell, has some ridiculously small maps, and doesn't have nearly enough enemies. The campaign only has eight maps unless you buy the DLC, and whatever story there is isn't engaging at all. I got enough skill points after half the game to fill all the useful skills. The healing skills were almost never used, because the enemy AI is dumb as hell!

On top of all that, it's STILL a pain in the neck to check your "service record" to see which collectibles you've gotten.

Rebellion, it's pretty clear you're just phoning it in at this point. Either quit the franchise and make something else, or put some real effort into your next Sniper Elite game.

Please.
Fun Gameplay. Always Enjoy Killing Natzis.

It’s a solid game— Forget standing in one spot like it’s a budget arcade shooter. The maps are wide open, packed with objectives, kill targets, collectibles, and enough side content to derail your original plan within five minutes. You’re not playing—you’re stalking. Best comparison? Imagine GTA and Hitman had a slightly unhinged child raised on a strict diet of anti-1940s Germany sentiment. That’s the vibe. The weapons feel authentic, and the difficulty settings actually matter. Crank it up to the highest level and suddenly you’re not a gamer anymore—you’re doing maths. Wind, distance, bullet drop… miss your shot and it’s entirely your fault. As part of the franchise, it’s a win. There’s a ton of content, the atmosphere is great, and if you grab it on sale, it feels like you’ve robbed the developers (in a good way). These games are easily 200+ hour time sinks if you let them be. Also, after enough playtime, you will start understanding shouted German commands—which is either immersive or mildly concerning.
